m130: Which photos and videos can I import?
m131: SD Card Import recognizes common RAW, JPEG, and video formats. The scan also shows camera metadata sidecars and unsupported files, so you can review what is on the card. See the {0}guide{/0} for the full workflow.
m132: What happens if I import the same card again?
m133: SD Card Import recognizes files recorded in its import history and skips repeat copies. The review shows what’s new and what’s already imported before you begin.
m135: Into the destination folders you choose. You can keep photos and videos together, use separate destinations, and organize by capture date. Review the planned paths before copying.
m136: Does SD Card Import delete anything from my card?
m137: SD Card Import copies your media without automatically deleting the originals from the source card. When the import finishes, you can safely eject a supported removable card.
m138: How do the two editions differ?
m139: The direct download linked here is free and open source under the MIT License. You can download the signed app or explore the {0}source on GitHub{/0}. SD Card Import, the App Store edition, includes one completed import free, then a one-time $9.99 U.S. purchase for unlimited imports with Family Sharing. Scanning and previewing remain free.
m140: What do I need to get started?
m141: A Mac running macOS 14 or newer, a mounted card or source folder, and enough space in your destination. Install SD Card Import from the App Store and choose your folders. The {0}install guide{/0} covers both editions.

m253: How SD Import and SD Card Import store data locally and handle diagnostics, updates, and purchases.
m255: Last updated: 2026-09-10. This policy covers SD Import (direct download) and SD Card Import (App Store edition), local macOS utilities for copying photos and videos from SD cards or selected source folders.
m257: Both editions store app settings, folder permissions, import history, and records used to skip duplicate imports locally on your Mac. The direct edition uses {0}. SD Card Import uses a local App Group container shared with its card-detection helper. Both may also store ordinary preferences through macOS UserDefaults.
m259: If you enable portable import receipts, the app creates or appends {0} on writable sources. The hidden ledger contains versioned file fingerprints, relative source paths, sizes, modification and import timestamps, and validation checksums so another Mac can avoid duplicate imports. It does not contain destination paths, usernames, or media contents. The option is disabled by default, read-only sources continue without writing portable history, and ledger access refuses symbolic-link redirection outside the selected source.
m261: The direct edition uses Sparkle for update checks when configured in the installed release. These checks contact the GitHub Release-hosted appcast for this repository. SD Card Import receives updates through the App Store and does not include Sparkle.
m263: Apple processes purchases and restores for SD Card Import. The app uses StoreKit transaction and entitlement information to determine purchase access. It stores purchase-access state and free-import usage locally. We do not receive payment card details.
m265: Neither edition sends analytics, telemetry, import history, media files, folder listings, or crash reports to the maintainer. Diagnostics export is opt-in and redacted. The direct edition can reveal the macOS crash-report folder or export the latest local app crash report. The App Store edition cannot browse system crash reports. Neither edition uploads crash reports automatically.
m267: Public GitHub issues are visible to everyone. Do not attach private photos, videos, full card dumps, credentials, or unredacted logs to public issues.
